origNote: 問題はBabel Flightのオリジナルです(2026年1月からの新形式に合わせています)。
markNote: 採点は本番のスコア(1〜6)とは違う、自分でつける目安です。
voiceNote: 英語はこの端末の音声で読み上げます。本番は録音の音声なので、聞き返し(Pardon?)はできません。
subNote: インタビューの質問を表示する(本番は画面にも出ます)
sumNote: 本番は1〜6のバンドで評価されます(必要なスコアは大学や機関によって違います)。70%をこえたら手ごたえあり。
againNote: リピートの場面は変わります
flow: Listen and Repeat ・ 1つの場面の英文7つを、聞いたとおりにくり返す(準備なし・英文は表示されない)
Take an Interview ・ 1つのテーマについての質問4つに、それぞれ45秒で答える(準備なし)

open.t: This is the Speaking section. There are two tasks. In the first task, you will hear seven sentences. After each one, repeat exactly what you heard.

close.t: This is the end of the Speaking section.

steps.t: Take an Interview. You have agreed to take part in a research study about how students use technology for learning. A researcher will interview you online.
First, can you tell me about a piece of technology you use for studying, and how you use it?
Some students prefer to read on paper, while others prefer reading on a screen. Which do you prefer, and why?
Have you ever had a problem with technology during a class or an exam? What happened?
Some people think schools should limit how much students use phones in class. Do you agree? Why or why not?

i1.q: First, can you tell me about a piece of technology you use for studying, and how you use it?
i1.ja: 勉強に使っている機器と、その使い方を教えてください。
model: I mostly use a vocabulary app on my phone. Every morning on the train, I review about thirty words. The app shows me the words I often forget more frequently, so it's very efficient. I also use my laptop to watch online lectures when I don't understand something in class.
points: 最初の1文で答えをはっきり
理由 + 具体例(体験)で45秒を使い切る
最後にひとことまとめる

i2.q: Some students prefer to read on paper, while others prefer reading on a screen. Which do you prefer, and why?
i2.ja: 紙で読むのと画面で読むの、どちらが好きですか。理由も。
model: I prefer reading on paper, especially for difficult texts. I can write notes in the margins and I remember the information better. Reading on a screen is convenient for short articles, but after an hour my eyes get tired and I start checking messages instead of reading.
points: 最初の1文で答えをはっきり
理由 + 具体例(体験)で45秒を使い切る
最後にひとことまとめる

i3.q: Have you ever had a problem with technology during a class or an exam? What happened?
i3.ja: 授業や試験中に機器のトラブルがあったことはありますか。
model: Yes. During an online English test, my Internet connection suddenly stopped. I was very nervous, but I contacted the teacher by phone, and she let me restart the test later. Since then, I always charge my devices and check the connection before important classes.
points: 最初の1文で答えをはっきり
理由 + 具体例(体験)で45秒を使い切る
最後にひとことまとめる

i4.q: Some people think schools should limit how much students use phones in class. Do you agree? Why or why not?
i4.ja: 授業中のスマホ利用を学校が制限すべきだという意見に賛成ですか。
model: I partly agree. Phones can be distracting, because students check social media instead of listening. However, phones are also useful tools, for example for looking up words. So I think teachers should decide when phones can be used, rather than banning them completely.
points: 最初の1文で答えをはっきり
理由 + 具体例(体験)で45秒を使い切る
最後にひとことまとめる

steps.t: Take an Interview. Your university is collecting opinions about student life. A staff member from the student center will ask you some questions.
First, how do you usually spend your time between classes?
Would you rather live in a dormitory on campus or in an apartment off campus? Why?
Tell me about a club or activity you have joined. What did you get out of it?
Some people say students should have a part-time job while they are studying. What do you think?

i1.q: First, how do you usually spend your time between classes?
i1.ja: 授業の合間はふだんどう過ごしていますか。
model: Usually I go to the library and review my notes from the previous class. If I have a long break, I meet my friends at the cafeteria. Sometimes I also go to the gym for a short workout, because it helps me focus in the afternoon.
points: 最初の1文で答えをはっきり
理由 + 具体例(体験)で45秒を使い切る
最後にひとことまとめる

i2.q: Would you rather live in a dormitory on campus or in an apartment off campus? Why?
i2.ja: キャンパス内の寮と、キャンパス外のアパート、どちらに住みたいですか。
model: I'd rather live in a dormitory, at least in my first year. It's close to classes, so I wouldn't waste time commuting. It's also a great way to make friends from different countries, which would help me improve my English quickly.
points: 最初の1文で答えをはっきり
理由 + 具体例(体験)で45秒を使い切る
最後にひとことまとめる

i3.q: Tell me about a club or activity you have joined. What did you get out of it?
i3.ja: 参加したクラブや活動と、そこで得たことを教えてください。
model: In junior high school, I joined the science club. We built small model rockets and tested them on the school field. Through this activity, I learned how to work in a team and how to deal with failure, because our rockets didn't fly well at first.
points: 最初の1文で答えをはっきり
理由 + 具体例(体験)で45秒を使い切る
最後にひとことまとめる

i4.q: Some people say students should have a part-time job while they are studying. What do you think?
i4.ja: 学生はアルバイトをするべきだという意見について、どう思いますか。
model: I think a part-time job can be valuable if it's only a few hours a week. Students learn responsibility and how to communicate with customers. But if they work too much, their grades may suffer, so they need to balance work and study carefully.
points: 最初の1文で答えをはっきり
理由 + 具体例(体験)で45秒を使い切る
最後にひとことまとめる

steps.t: Take an Interview. A travel magazine is writing an article about young people and travel. A reporter will interview you.
First, tell me about a place you have visited that you would recommend to others.
When you travel, do you prefer to plan everything in advance or decide things as you go? Why?
Have you ever had a problem while traveling? How did you deal with it?
Do you think young people should travel abroad before they start working? Why or why not?

i1.q: First, tell me about a place you have visited that you would recommend to others.
i1.ja: ほかの人にすすめたい、行ったことのある場所を教えてください。
model: I'd recommend Okinawa. The beaches are beautiful, and the water is so clear that you can see fish without diving. I also enjoyed learning about its history and culture, which are quite different from the rest of Japan. The food is great too.
points: 最初の1文で答えをはっきり
理由 + 具体例(体験)で45秒を使い切る
最後にひとことまとめる

i2.q: When you travel, do you prefer to plan everything in advance or decide things as you go? Why?
i2.ja: 旅行では事前に全部計画するのと、その場で決めるのとどちらが好きですか。
model: I prefer to plan the main things in advance, like transportation and hotels, because it saves time and stress. But I like to leave some free time each day to explore, because the best experiences often happen when you don't expect them.
points: 最初の1文で答えをはっきり
理由 + 具体例(体験)で45秒を使い切る
最後にひとことまとめる

i3.q: Have you ever had a problem while traveling? How did you deal with it?
i3.ja: 旅行中に困ったことはありますか。どう対処しましたか。
model: Once our flight was delayed for four hours because of a typhoon. At first I was frustrated, but I watched the planes and chatted with the airline staff. They explained how pilots decide whether it's safe to fly, which was actually really interesting.
points: 最初の1文で答えをはっきり
理由 + 具体例(体験)で45秒を使い切る
最後にひとことまとめる

i4.q: Do you think young people should travel abroad before they start working? Why or why not?
i4.ja: 若者は働き始める前に海外へ行くべきだと思いますか。
model: Yes, I do. Traveling abroad helps young people become more independent and open-minded. They have to communicate in another language and solve problems by themselves. These experiences are useful in almost any job, especially in international companies.
points: 最初の1文で答えをはっきり
理由 + 具体例(体験)で45秒を使い切る
最後にひとことまとめる

steps.t: Take an Interview. You are taking part in a study about how students manage their time. A researcher will ask you a few questions.
First, can you describe a typical weekday for you?
Do you prefer to study in the morning or at night? Why?
Tell me about a time when you had too much to do. How did you handle it?
Some people say it is better to study for long periods without breaks. Do you agree?

i1.q: First, can you describe a typical weekday for you?
i1.ja: ふだんの平日の過ごし方を説明してください。
model: I get up at six thirty and leave for school at seven thirty. Classes finish around three, and then I have club activities until five. After dinner I study for about two hours, and I usually go to bed around eleven.
points: 最初の1文で答えをはっきり
理由 + 具体例(体験)で45秒を使い切る
最後にひとことまとめる

i2.q: Do you prefer to study in the morning or at night? Why?
i2.ja: 朝に勉強するのと夜に勉強するの、どちらが好きですか。
model: I prefer studying in the morning, even though it's hard to wake up. My mind is fresh, and there are fewer distractions because my friends aren't sending messages yet. At night I'm often tired, so I only do easy review then.
points: 最初の1文で答えをはっきり
理由 + 具体例(体験)で45秒を使い切る
最後にひとことまとめる

i3.q: Tell me about a time when you had too much to do. How did you handle it?
i3.ja: やることが多すぎたときのことと、どう乗り切ったかを教えてください。
model: Last winter I had exams, a speech contest and a club event in the same week. I made a list of everything and decided what was most urgent. I also asked my teacher for advice on the speech. It was tough, but I finished everything on time.
points: 最初の1文で答えをはっきり
理由 + 具体例(体験)で45秒を使い切る
最後にひとことまとめる

i4.q: Some people say it is better to study for long periods without breaks. Do you agree?
i4.ja: 休憩なしで長時間勉強するほうがよいという意見に賛成ですか。
model: No, I don't agree. When I study for too long without a break, I stop understanding what I read. I find it more effective to study for about fifty minutes and then rest for ten. Short breaks help me stay focused for the whole day.
points: 最初の1文で答えをはっきり
理由 + 具体例(体験)で45秒を使い切る
最後にひとことまとめる

steps.t: Take an Interview. A university is planning a new program about careers. An advisor will interview you about your goals.
First, what kind of job are you interested in, and why?
Who has given you the most useful advice about your future? What did they say?
Would you prefer to work for a large company or a small one? Why?
Some people think it is important to choose a career early, while others think it is better to wait. What do you think?

i1.q: First, what kind of job are you interested in, and why?
i1.ja: どんな仕事に興味がありますか。理由も。
model: I'm interested in becoming an airline pilot. I've loved airplanes since I was a child, and I like the idea of a job that combines technology, teamwork and travel. It's also a job where English is used every day, which I enjoy.
points: 最初の1文で答えをはっきり
理由 + 具体例(体験)で45秒を使い切る
最後にひとことまとめる

i2.q: Who has given you the most useful advice about your future? What did they say?
i2.ja: 将来について、いちばん役に立つアドバイスをくれたのはだれですか。
model: My uncle gave me the most useful advice. He works for a trading company, and he told me that English is just a tool, and what matters is what you can do with it. Since then, I've tried to learn about science and aviation in English, not just the language.
points: 最初の1文で答えをはっきり
理由 + 具体例(体験)で45秒を使い切る
最後にひとことまとめる

i3.q: Would you prefer to work for a large company or a small one? Why?
i3.ja: 大企業と小さな会社、どちらで働きたいですか。
model: I'd prefer a large company. Large companies usually offer better training programs, which is important for a job like pilot. They also have more chances to work abroad. On the other hand, I understand that small companies can give you responsibility earlier.
points: 最初の1文で答えをはっきり
理由 + 具体例(体験)で45秒を使い切る
最後にひとことまとめる

i4.q: Some people think it is important to choose a career early, while others think it is better to wait. What do you think?
i4.ja: 進路を早く決めるべきか、待つべきか、どう思いますか。
model: I think it's good to have a goal early, because you can prepare step by step. For example, I've been studying English with my goal in mind. However, people should stay flexible, because they may discover new interests along the way.
points: 最初の1文で答えをはっきり
理由 + 具体例(体験)で45秒を使い切る
最後にひとことまとめる
